source_text: Ἄθεοι μὲν οὖν ὡς οὔκ ἐσμεν, τὸν δημιουργὸν τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς σεβόμενοι, ἀνενδεῆ αἱμάτων καὶ σπονδῶν καὶ θυμιαμάτων, ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν, λέγοντες, λόγῳ εὐχῆς καὶ εὐχαριστίας ἐφ᾿ οἷς προσφερόμεθα πᾶσιν, ὅση δύναμις, αἰνοῦντες, μόνην ἀξίαν αὐτοῦ τιμὴν ταύτην παραλαβόντες, τὸ τὰ ὑπ᾿ ἐκείνου εἰς διατροφὴν γενόμενα οὐ πυρὶ δαπανᾶν, ἀλλ᾿ ἑαυτοῖς καὶ τοῖς δεομένοις προσφέρειν, ἐκείνῳ δὲ εὐχαρίστους ὄντας διὰ λόγου πομπὰς καὶ ὕμνους πέμπειν ὑπέρ τε τοῦ γεγονέναι καὶ τῶν εἰς εὐρωστίαν πόρων πάντων, ποιοτήτων μὲν γενῶν καὶ μεταβολῶν ὡρῶν, καὶ τοῦ πάλιν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ γενέσθαι διὰ πίστιν τὴν ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτήσεις πέμποντες, — τίς σωφρονῶν οὐχ ὁμολογήσει; Τὸν διδάσκαλόν τε τούτων γενόμενον ἡμῖν καὶ εἰς τοῦτο γεννηθέντα Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν σταυρωθέντα ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, τοῦ γενομένου ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ ἐπὶ χρόνοις Τιβερίου Καίσαρος ἐπιτρόπου, υἱὸν αὐτὸν τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ μαθόντες καὶ ἐν δευτέρᾳ χώρᾳ ἔχοντες, πνεῦμά τε προφητικὸν ἐν τρίτῃ τάξει ὅτι μετὰ λόγου τιμῶμεν, ἀποδείξομεν. Ἐνταῦθα γὰρ μανίαν ἡμῶν καταφαίνονται, δευτέραν χώραν μετὰ τὸν ἄτρεπτον καὶ ἀεὶ ὄντα θεὸν καὶ γεννήτορα τῶν ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπῳ σταυρωθέντι διδόναι ἡμᾶς λέγοντες, ἀγνοοῦντες τὸ ἐν τούτῳ μυστήριον, ᾧ προσέχειν ὑμᾶς ἐξηγουμένων ἡμῶν προτρεπόμεθα.
pass_a_gloss: Atheists, then, as we are not, revering the Creator of all this universe, being without need of blood and libations and incense, as we have been taught, saying, with word of prayer and thanksgiving for the things we offer to all, as much as we are able, praising, having received this honor alone worthy of Him, not to squander on fire the things that have come into being under Him for nourishment, but to offer them to ourselves and to those in need, and being grateful to Him, sending through word processions and hymns on behalf of what has come to be and all the things that bring prosperity, of the kinds of goods and changes of seasons, and of being born again in incorruption through faith, making requests to Him — who, being sane, will not confess? We have Jesus Christ, who has become our teacher of these things and was born for this purpose, the Christ who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, who was in Judea during the times of Tiberius Caesar, the governor, having learned that He is the Son of the truly existing God and holding Him in second place, and the prophetic Spirit in third order, because we honor the Word, we will demonstrate. For here, indeed, our madness is revealed, giving second place to a man who was crucified after the unchangeable and always existing God and Father of all things, saying this, being ignorant of the mystery in this, to which we urge you to pay attention as we explain.

pass_b_english: People call us atheists, but we are not; we revere the Creator of this whole universe, who stands in no need of blood, libations, or incense. As we have been taught, we honor Him with the word of prayer and thanksgiving over whatever we are able to offer, praising Him because we have received this alone as the honor worthy of Him: not to burn up on fire the things that have come into being under Him for nourishment, but to offer them to ourselves and to those in need, and in gratitude to send up to Him, through the word, processions and hymns on behalf of creation itself, on behalf of all that brings prosperity — the kinds of produce and the changes of the seasons — and on behalf of being born again in incorruption through faith, as we make our requests to Him. Who, being in their right mind, would not confess this?

We have come to know Jesus Christ as the teacher of these things and the one born for this very purpose, the Christ crucified under Pontius Pilate, procurator in Judea in the time of Tiberius Caesar. We have learned that He is the Son of the truly existing God, and we hold Him in second place, and the prophetic Spirit in third rank, because we honor the Word; and we will demonstrate this. For it is here that our madness is laid bare in the eyes of our critics: they say we give second place after the unchangeable, ever‑existing God and Father of all things to a man who was crucified, and they say this in ignorance of the mystery contained in it. To that mystery we urge you to give attention as we explain it.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek, particularly the long periodic sentence regarding the offerings and the subsequent theological hierarchy. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source. Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of the rhetorical question and the final clause without introducing new meaning or omitting the distinction between the 'second place' and 'third order'.

The Greek text is accurately translated in Pass A and Pass B. The title 'Response to Accusation of Atheism' correctly captures the thought of the passage. All key elements of the original Greek are preserved, including the negation ('Ἄθεοι μὲν οὖν ὡς οὔκ ἐσμεν'), the agency ('we revere the Creator'), the modality ('as we have been taught'), the doctrine ('Jesus Christ, the Son of the truly existing God'), and the scripture citations (none explicitly quoted, but the content aligns with the theological context).
